messages:
Mateo: heads-up — we started seeing a spike (~2.3k) in tool schema_rejects for the web-search tool after the strict validation rollout at 15:00 UTC. runtime routed ~18% to fallback model.
Priya R: saw that, dashboard shows a blob of rejects from a single customer integration. looks like malformed JSON in fncall payloads.
Alex B: quick question — are we charging customers for requests that get schema_rejected then routed to fallback? customers just pinged support.
Jin: runtime currently increments 'requests' and 'tool_invokes' always; schema_reject is a separate telemetry counter. we do NOT decrement quota on validation failures today.
Mateo: customer reported they were billed for retries. maybe retrying happened client-side, so they were billed. unclear.
Priya R: UI-wise customers just see 200 + content, so they don't know we rejected an internal toolcall. we should surface an explicit flag in console for 'schema_rejects' on per-route logs. :eyes:
Alex B: my opinion: charging for totally rejected outputs is surprising. if we fallback automatically to another model and return an answer, we probably should count the final served tokens only. if we surface the reject we could show sample and explain billing.
Jin: implementation constraints: validation happens post-token-generation for some models (we validate tool output shape after decoding). two options: 1) mark as 'pre-serve reject' and abort (cheaper) 2) post-serve reject + fallback (expensive). current canary did (2) for strict compatibility.
Mateo: example payload we see in logs:
```json
{
  "error": "schema_mismatch",
  "expected": "ToolResult",
  "received": "\"string\"",
  "route": "web-search-v2",
  "validation_level": "strict"
}
```
Priya R: telemetry ask: add tag `reject_phase: post_decode|pre_decode` and `reject_reason` string, plus sample the rejected output (1%) and attach to trace. also surface a counter in per-route dashboard.
Eva (obs-bot): logged event: metrics.increment("tool.schema_reject", 1, {route: "web-search-v2", level: "strict"})
Alex B: UX ask: add an explicit column in routes table: "Schema rejects / 1k reqs" and a link to sample viewer. Also a toggle to treat rejects as billing-blocking or not for enterprise tenants.
Jin: engineering plan: revert strict canary to soft-validate for 1hr while we add telemetry + sampling. add quick rollout flag so ops can flip validation to `soft` per-customer.
Mateo: agreement: do that. action items:
- Jin: add `reject_phase` tag + 1% body sampling to trace pipeline (ETA 6h).
- Priya R: design console card for schema rejects and billing toggle (ETA EOD).
- Alex B: draft customer-facing note clarifying how billing interacts with rejects (ETA tomorrow).
- Mateo: temp rollback of strict canary to soft validate (doing now). ops-bot: kick deploy.
ops-bot: deploy triggered: rollback/strict-validate -> soft-validate on canary (id: canary-42).
Priya R: one more thought — for routing policy: if we do post-decode reject -> fallback, should fallback count as the same request for quota/SLAs? leaning no for billing, yes for SLA.
Alex B: agreed: SLA vs billing split makes sense. mark as "served_by_fallback" in traces for SLO math.
Jin: I'll push a small patch with a config snippet we can toggle per-route:
```yaml
validation:
  level: strict|soft
  on_reject: abort|fallback|surface
  bill_on_reject: true|false
```
Mateo: perfect. after Jin's patch + telemetry sampling we'll run a 5% canary for 24h and monitor `tool.schema_reject` and `fallback_rate`.
Priya R: thanks — will add a card to the console backlog and wire design mocks to the sample viewer once telemetry is in. :thumbsup:
Alex B: ping me when the customer note is ready, I'll review.
Jin: starting the rollback and instrument work now. will post updates here.
Mateo: thanks team — closing this thread when canary is stable and telemetry landed.
